body: 40 g, 8 cm carapace width. Low, rounded cephalothorax; broad abdomen; eight short, gripping legs; two modified chelicerae for shredding.

chains.trait: Low, calcified carapace shields against wave shock.
links: Carapace minimizes drag and anchors body during surges.
Wave forces and desiccation at the wrack line demand protection.
3.2 m tides amplify surge on the shelf (F13); dense air increases spray impact (D11).
Basalt and andesite cliffs (F9) channel water into the wrack line.

skill.effect: +50% resist wave damage and wind gusts; reduces knockback.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to crushing from above; shell limits flexibility.
observe: Legs tucked tightly under shell during surf bursts.
Hides under wrack clumps when tide recedes fast.

journal.en: It wears a shell against the sea's hammer.

plausibility.summary: A low, broad calcified exoskeleton at the wrack line matches intertidal hydrodynamics: surge and splash, not constant deep surf, dominate at shelf resonance (F13); a rounded, low-profile body reduces lift and drag in swash (Denny’s wave-swept-intertidal framework). At ~40 g and ~8 cm it is in the size class of shore crabs and large isopods that shelter under wrack and in crevices. Dense air (F4/D11) mainly raises aerodynamic load on exposed animals during gusts; it does not negate the need for a hard dorsal shield against abrasion from basalt grit (F9) and tumbling debris.

At ~40 g and ~8 cm it is in the size class of shore crabs and large isopods that shelter under wrack and in crevices. Dense air (F4/D11) mainly raises aerodynamic load on exposed animals during gusts; it does not negate the need for a hard dorsal shield against abrasion from basalt grit (F9) and tumbling debris.

analogues.organism: Rocky-shore grapsoid/ocypodid crabs and littoral isopods (Ligia): low posture, hard carapace/telson, refuge under wrack during retreating tides.

chains.trait: Eight gripping legs with hydrophobic bristles.
links: Legs splayed for stability; bristles repel water film.
Traction required on wet basalt and slimy wrack.
Volcanic rock is smooth; algae films reduce friction (F9, F20).
Eight legs provide a wide base; redundancy prevents falls on uneven terrain.

skill.effect: Move steadily on wet slopes up to 40° without slipping; +20% speed on shore.

chains.weakness: Cannot climb dry vertical rock; bristles mat in thick mud.
observe: Bristles repel water droplets in macro.
Legs splayed wide for stability on slope.
Climbs vertical basalt face where water films exist.

journal.en: Eight legs grip what two would lose.

links: Forages at night; ignores visual bait.
Exploits longer-lasting scent trails to find hidden wrack patches.
Dense air and high oxygen slow molecular diffusion (D8, D10).
Scent trails persist 1.6× longer in still air (F16).

skill.effect: Locate food sources within 10 m in darkness or fog; +15% befriend chance via calm movement.

chains.weakness: Bright light or strong wind breaks the trail; deaf to high pitches.
observe: Forages only after sunset or in heavy fog.
Ignores shiny objects but tracks carcass scent.

journal.en: Night is its canvas; scent is its eye.

plausibility.summary: Rewrite sensors as pedipalp/leg tarsal chemo- and mechanoreceptors (or foreleg ‘feelers’), not antennae. Cite D18+F16 for scent, not D10. Keep ‘deaf to high pitches’ as optional flavour only if you add a low-frequency predator cue—not required for plausibility.

chains.trait: Gut flora metabolizes reduced sulfur and toxins.
links: Safe consumption of decaying matter near seeps.
Wrack accumulates decay products and volcanic gases.
Vent gases and seeps concentrate H₂S and arsenic (F22, F23).
One biochemistry allows gut symbionts to share pathways (F24).

skill.effect: +20 health when eating rotting carcass or sulfurous wrack; immune to mild poison.

chains.weakness: Sulfur breath alerts carnivores; cannot digest fresh meat without rot.
observe: Greenish gut visible through translucent abdomen.

journal.en: Poison is just flavor to its gut.

plausibility.summary: Limit passive effect to rotting carcass/sulfurous wrack and weathered crust flakes, not active vent mats. Replace ‘immune to mild poison’ with reduced penalty from H₂S/arsenic in wrack, with costra_de_azufre as rare buff item. Translucent abdomen showing ‘greenish gut’ is fine if mark as highly speculative visual.

body_plan.origin: Convergent arthropod radiation; high-leg count stabilizes on wet volcanic substrate.

secrets: A Pataosca carrying `costra_de_azufre` on its carapace unlocks 'Sulfur Gland' (fire resistance).
A Pataosca near a `pan_de_humus` patch reveals 'Fungal Symbiont' (passive regen).
moments: On a moonless night, a Pataosca freezes, legs splayed, sensing a predator's footfall inches away before the shadow falls.

journal.en: Legs splayed, it waits in the wrack until the sun burns the fog.
It turns dead algae into life, leaving nothing to waste.
